verdict: Crown Castle's revenue fell 7% as the DISH and Sprint tenant exits shrank tower rents, but lower interest costs after selling its fiber business still pushed AFFO per share up 11%.

kpis.label: Site rental revenue
kpis.note: -5% YoY; organic billings +3.5% before DISH/Sprint exits

segments.name: Site rental
segments.note: Rent from mobile carriers putting antennas on Crown Castle's towers. Billings grew 3.5% organically, but DISH terminations (-$61M) and Sprint cancellations (-$5M) versus last year's billings, plus lower straight-line rent, pulled reported revenue down.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Work installing and upgrading carriers' equipment on towers — much smaller since Crown Castle sold its fiber and small-cell businesses and became a pure tower company.

opex.name: Depreciation, amortization & accretion
opex.note: The towers and land rights wearing out on paper over time — a big non-cash cost for a tower owner, and the main reason GAAP profit looks small next to AFFO.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — down from $97M a year ago on cost savings.

opex.name: Restructuring charges
opex.note: Costs of reshaping the company after the fiber and small-cell sale.

opex.name: Asset write-down charges
opex.note: Writing down assets that are worth less than their book value.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $177M (net of deferred financing cost amortization) on Crown Castle's debt, plus $3M of interest income and a $3M other expense — net -$177M.
oneTimers: Restructuring charges of $6M and asset write-down charges of $1M are included in GAAP results this quarter.

There were no discontinued-operations results in Q3 2026. For the nine months, the sold fiber and small-cell businesses contributed $350M of income before a $625M loss on disposal — that disposal loss does not touch this quarter.

takeaways.title: Tenant exits are the drag
takeaways.text: Site rental revenue fell to $966M. The underlying towers business grew — organic billings +3.5%, or +3.8% excluding DISH from last year — but losing DISH and Sprint as tenants removed $66M of billings versus a year ago.

takeaways.title: AFFO rose anyway
takeaways.text: AFFO — the cash-style profit REIT investors watch, which adds back tower depreciation — rose 8% to $530M, and 11% per share to $1.24, helped by lower interest expense and fewer shares after the fiber sale proceeds were put to work.

takeaways.title: The guide went up a notch
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA eased to $673M from $718M, but Crown Castle still raised its full-year 2026 guide — Adjusted EBITDA by $25M and AFFO by $5M — citing ground-lease buyouts, cost savings and a new customer agreement.
